How to make your RAG prototype prod-ready (Sponsor)

Getting a RAG demo running takes an afternoon. Getting it to perform at scale is considerably harder.

运行一个 RAG（检索增强生成，Retrieval-Augmented Generation）演示只需一个下午。但要让它在大规模场景下良好运行则困难得多。

Algolia's whitepapercovers the engineering decisions that matter:

Algolia 的白皮书涵盖了重要的工程决策：

  1. How to split documents without losing context (and why 10–20% overlap is the sweet spot),
  2. Which vector indexing strategy fits your scale,
  3. How to assemble prompts that actually ground LLM outputs.

  1. 如何在分割文档时不丢失上下文（以及为什么 10–20% 的重叠是最佳点），
  2. 哪种向量索引（vector indexing）策略适合你的规模，
  3. 如何组装能够真正为 LLM（大语言模型）输出提供依据的提示词。

It also gets into thestuff that's easy to overlook: PII tokenization, encryption for vector stores, and compliance frameworks for handling enterprise data in RAG pipelines.

它还深入探讨了那些容易被忽视的内容：PII（个人可识别信息，Personally Identifiable Information）分词、向量存储的加密，以及在 RAG 流程中处理企业数据的合规框架。

Written by the team behind 1.75 trillion annual searches.

由每年处理 1.75 万亿次搜索的团队撰写。

OpenAI Agreement with the Department of War (4 minute read)

OpenAI announced a classified deployment agreement with the US Department of War that included explicit red lines against mass surveillance, autonomous weapons control, and high-stakes automated decision-making.

OpenAI 宣布与美国 Department of War（战争部）达成一项机密部署协议，其中包括明确禁止大规模监控、自主武器控制以及高风险自动化决策的红线（red lines）。

OpenAI raises $110B (3 minute read)

OpenAI announced a $110 billion funding round at a $730 billion pre-money valuation backed by Amazon, Nvidia, and SoftBank to expand compute, distribution, and enterprise infrastructure. The company now supports 900 million weekly active users, 50 million consumer subscribers, 9 million paying business users, and 1.6 million weekly Codex developers, extending AI use deep into workflows across business functions. This capital and strategic cloud partnerships aim to shift frontier AI from research to global production scale with broader enterprise and developer adoption.

OpenAI 宣布完成一轮 1100 亿美元的融资，投前估值达 7300 亿美元，由 Amazon、Nvidia 和 SoftBank 支持，用于扩展计算、分发和企业基础设施。该公司目前拥有 9 亿周活跃用户、5000 万消费者订阅者、900 万付费企业用户，以及每周 160 万 Codex 开发者，将 AI 应用深入到各业务职能的工作流程中。这笔资金和战略性云合作伙伴关系旨在将前沿 AI 从研究阶段推向全球生产规模，并实现更广泛的企业和开发者采用。

Google tests new Learning Hub powered by goal-based actions (2 minute read)

Google accidentally revealed a new Gemini feature, "Goal Scheduled Actions," that allows AI to autonomously adjust tasks toward defined objectives. This contrasts with existing scheduled actions that repeat fixed prompts. The feature aligns with Google's LearnLM initiative, suggesting applications in education, where structured AI guidance could aid skill development.

Google 意外泄露了一项新的 Gemini 功能——"Goal Scheduled Actions"（目标定时动作），该功能允许 AI 自主调整任务以实现既定目标。这与重复固定提示词的现有定时动作形成对比。该功能与 Google 的 LearnLM 计划一致，暗示其在教育领域的应用，其中结构化 AI 指导可能有助于技能发展。

Claude for Chrome Extension Internals (v1.0.56) (15 minute read)

This article looks at how Anthropic's Claude for Chrome extension works under the hood. The extension is a Chrome Manifest V3 extension built with React. It uses Anthropic's JavaScript SDK directly in the browser, opening as a side panel alongside the active tab. The agent can see and interact with web pages.

本文探讨了 Anthropic 的 Claude for Chrome 扩展的内部工作原理。该扩展是一个使用 React 构建的 Chrome Manifest V3 扩展。它直接在浏览器中使用 Anthropic 的 JavaScript SDK（软件开发工具包），作为侧边栏与活动标签页并排打开。该智能体（agent）可以查看并与网页交互。

"All Lawful Use": Much More Than You Wanted To Know (18 minute read)

Anthropic was recently declared a supply chain risk due to its refusal to allow the Department of War to use its technology for mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. A few hours later, the Department of War announced a partnership with OpenAI. While OpenAI and the Department of War have tried to assure the public that they won't use AI for mass surveillance and autonomous weaponry, there are wide loopholes in current laws against their use. The Department of War is also able to change many of the rules that currently exist at any time.

Anthropic 最近被宣布为供应链风险，因为它拒绝允许战争部将其技术用于大规模监控和自主武器。几小时后，战争部宣布与 OpenAI 建立合作伙伴关系。虽然 OpenAI 和战争部试图向公众保证不会将 AI 用于大规模监控和自主武器，但现行法律中存在大量漏洞。战争部还能够随时更改许多现行规则。

Why XML Tags Are so Fundamental to Claude (4 minute read)

Structuring prompts with XML can be a transformative experience in Claude. The AI's framework specifically incorporates XML tags as key elements. The repurposing of XML technology may be a core aspect of what makes Claude distinctive. It gives Claude the ability to distinguish between the transition from first-order to second-order expressions, which is a mechanism fundamentally required for information transfer between any two entities. Claude's awareness of the concept of delimiters is crucial to every processing and communication of information, and it is this capacity that makes Claude so effective at interpreting layered meaning.

在 Claude 中使用 XML 结构化提示词可以带来变革性的体验。该 AI 的框架特别将 XML 标签作为关键元素融入。XML 技术的重新利用可能是使 Claude 独具特色的核心方面。它赋予 Claude 区分从一阶到二阶表达式转换的能力，这是任何两个实体之间信息传输所根本需要的机制。Claude 对分隔符（delimiters）概念的认知对信息的每一次处理和通信都至关重要，正是这种能力使 Claude 在解释分层含义方面如此有效。

90% of Expert Work Can't Be Verified by Today's AI Training Methods (5 minute read)

Around 90% of expert work across healthcare, legal, finance, and engineering relies on subjective judgment, making it incompatible with current RLVR-style verification. To force verifiability, teams over-specify tasks and rubrics, turning real expert reasoning into shallow instruction-following and corrupting the training signal. Verification, not data scale, is the core bottleneck, and the winners will be those who can evaluate judgment-heavy, non-deterministic work without distorting it.

医疗、法律、金融和工程领域约 90% 的专家工作依赖于主观判断，使其与当前的 RLVR（可验证奖励强化学习，Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards）式验证不兼容。为了强制实现可验证性，团队过度指定任务和评分标准，将真正的专家推理转变为浅层的指令遵循，从而破坏了训练信号。验证（而非数据规模）是核心瓶颈，胜出者将是那些能够在不扭曲的情况下评估依赖判断的、非确定性工作的人。

👨‍💻

👨‍💻

You can't vibe code your way to a beautiful website (Sponsor)

And with , you don't have to. Hundreds of YC-backed founders use Framer to launch beautiful, production-ready sites in hours. It's a human-led, design-first answer to vibecoding that really works. Pre-seed and early stage startups get their first year free when they sign up.

而使用 Framer，你就不必如此。数百位 YC（Y Combinator）支持的创始人使用 Framer 在数小时内推出精美、可用于生产的网站。这是对 vibecoding（氛围编程）真正有效的人工主导、设计优先的解决方案。种子前和早期创业公司在注册时可免费使用第一年。

MCP is dead. Long live the CLI (4 minute read)

MCP is already dying. Major projects like OpenClaw and Pi don't support it for good reason. LLMs are really good at figuring out things on their own. All they really need is a command-line interface and some docs. CLIs are much more practical for both humans and agents. The tools already exist and are well-documented, and both humans and agents understand how to use them.

MCP（模型上下文协议，Model Context Protocol）已经在衰落。像 OpenClaw 和 Pi 这样的重大项目有充分的理由不支持它。LLM 非常擅长自主解决问题。它们真正需要的只是一个命令行界面（CLI，Command-Line Interface）和一些文档。CLI 对人类和智能体都更加实用。工具已经存在且有详细文档，人类和智能体都了解如何使用它们。

The Third Era of AI Software Development (3 minute read)

Cursor described a shift toward autonomous coding agents that operate over longer time horizons with minimal supervision, marking a "third era" of AI-assisted development. The company reported that over one-third of its merged pull requests were generated by cloud-based agents and outlined a future where developers manage fleets of agents rather than write code directly.

Cursor 描述了向自主编码智能体的转变，这些智能体在更长的时间范围内以最小监督运行，标志着 AI 辅助开发的"第三个时代"。该公司报告称，超过三分之一的合并拉取请求（pull requests）由基于云的智能体生成，并勾勒出一个未来图景：开发者管理智能体集群（fleets of agents），而非直接编写代码。

New agent-browser skill: Electron (1 minute read)

agent-browser can now control desktop apps built with Electron. It can also be used to debug Electron apps. agent-browser can be added to any coding agent. Popular Electron apps include Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify, and VS Code.

agent-browser 现在可以控制使用 Electron 构建的桌面应用。它也可用于调试 Electron 应用。agent-browser 可以添加到任何编码智能体中。流行的 Electron 应用包括 Discord、Figma、Notion、Spotify 和 VS Code。

Andrew Ng Says AGI Is Decades Away—and the Real AI Bubble Risk Is in the Training Layer (2 minute read)

Andrew Ng, founder of DeepLearning.AI and Coursera, executive chairman of Landing AI, and founding lead of the Google Brain team, says that AI capable of performing the full breadth of human intellectual tasks remains decades away. He recently appeared in an interview where he discussed enterprise adoption of agentic AI, whether AI is in a bubble, the AI infrastructure build-outs, geopolitical fragmentation and its effects on global AI strategy, and more. This post contains a transcript of that interview.

Andrew Ng（吴恩达），DeepLearning.AI 和 Coursera 创始人、Landing AI 执行董事长、Google Brain 团队创始负责人，表示能够执行人类全部智力任务的 AI（即 AGI，通用人工智能）仍需数十年才能实现。他最近在一次访谈中讨论了企业对 agentic AI（智能体 AI）的采用、AI 是否处于泡沫中、AI 基础设施建设、地缘政治碎片化及其对全球 AI 战略的影响等话题。本文包含该访谈的笔录。

When AI Labs Become Defense Contractors (8 minute read)

Government contacts offer predictable, multi-year, politically protected revenue streams that don't churn when a competitor releases a better model. Any lab serious about classified work has to build an organizational structure that meets government operational security requirements, and the lab that builds that structure first has a moat that no competitor can cross quickly. The defense budget is the largest single purchaser of advanced technology on the planet, and it's growing. Its multi-year contract cycles reward incumbents, and it's willing to use blunt regulatory tools against companies that don't cooperate.

政府合同提供可预测的、多年期的、受政治保护的收入流，不会因竞争对手发布更好的模型而流失。任何认真对待机密工作的实验室都必须建立满足政府运营安全要求的组织结构，而率先建立该结构的实验室将拥有竞争对手无法快速跨越的护城河（moat）。国防预算是全球最大的单一先进技术采购方，而且正在增长。其多年合同周期奖励现有供应商，并且愿意使用生硬的监管工具对付不合作的公司。

item.title: [翻译] Latent Space: 终结代码审查
item.description:
标签: #代码审查 #AI编程 #规范驱动

摘要: 本文指出，面对AI生成代码的指数级增长，传统人工代码审查已成为不可持续的瓶颈。作者主张将审查重心从"逐行检查代码实现"前移至"审查意图与规范定义"，通过多层自动化验证机制（包括多智能体竞争、确定性护栏、对抗性验证等）建立信任，实现人类无需阅读代码即可快速发布、观察、回滚的AI原生开发范式。

原标题: How to Kill the Code Review

Second wave speakers for AIE Europe and CFP for AIE World's Fair are announced today, and OpenCode is confirmed for Miami! We'll also be in Melbourne & Singapore.

AIE Europe（AI工程欧洲大会）的第二波演讲嘉宾和AIE World's Fair（AI工程世界博览会）的征稿启事今日发布，同时OpenCode迈阿密站已确认！我们还将前往墨尔本和新加坡。

Editor: This is the latest in our guest post program, where we will publish AI Engineering essays worth considering, even if we don't personally agree with them — having just shipped an AI review tool, this is one of those cases where I am not there yet, but is clearly on the horizon, and am happy for Ankit to argue the case!

编辑：这是我们客座文章计划的最新一篇，我们将发布值得思考的AI工程文章，即使我们个人并不完全认同——鉴于我们刚刚发布了一款AI审查工具（AI review tool），这正是那种我尚未完全接受但显然即将成为现实的观点，我很高兴让Ankit来阐述这一论点！

Humans already couldn't keep up with code review when humans wrote code at human speed. Every engineering org I've talked to has the same dirty secret: PRs sitting for days, rubber-stamp approvals, and reviewers skimming 500-line diffs because they have their own work to do.

当人类以人类的速度编写代码时，人类就已经跟不上代码审查（code review）的节奏了。我交谈过的每个工程团队都有同样的隐秘痛点：PR（Pull Request，拉取请求）积压数日、橡皮图章式的批准，以及审查者匆匆浏览500行代码差异（diff）因为他们自己也有工作要做。

We tell ourselves it is a quality gate, but teams have shipped without line-by-line review for decades. Code review wasn't even ubiquitous until around 2012-2014, one veteran engineer told me, there just aren't enough of us around to remember.

我们告诉自己这是质量门禁，但团队们在没有逐行审查的情况下已经交付了数十年。一位资深工程师告诉我，直到2012-2014年左右，代码审查才普及开来，只是经历过那个时代的人已经不多，无法记得了。

And even with reviews, things break. We have learned to build systems that handle failure because we accepted that review alone wasn't enough. This shows in terms of feature flags, rollouts, and instant rollbacks.

即使有审查，东西还是会坏。我们已经学会了构建能够处理故障的系统，因为我们接受了仅靠审查是不够的。这体现在功能标志（feature flags）、渐进式发布（rollouts）和即时回滚（instant rollbacks）等方面。

We have to give up on reading all the code

我们必须放弃阅读所有代码

Teams with high AI adoption complete 21% more tasks and merge 98% more pull requests, but PR review time increases 91%, based on data from over 10,000 developers across 1,255 teams.

根据来自1,255个团队的超过10,000名开发者的数据，高度采用AI的团队完成的任务多出21%，合并的拉取请求多出98%，但PR审查时间增加了91%。

Two things are scaling exponentially: the number of changes and the size of changes. We cannot consume this much code. Period. On top of that, developers keep saying that reviewing AI-generated code requires more effort than reviewing code written by their colleagues. Teams produce more code, then spend more time reviewing it.

有两样东西正在呈指数级增长：变更的数量和变更的规模。我们无法消化这么多代码。就这样。除此之外，开发者们不断表示，审查AI生成的代码比审查同事编写的代码需要更多精力。团队产出更多代码，然后花费更多时间审查它。

There is no way we win this fight with manual code reviews. Code review is a historical approval gate that no longer matches the shape of the work.

我们不可能通过人工代码审查赢得这场战斗。代码审查是一个历史遗留的批准门槛，已不再匹配当前工作的形态。

AI code review is still review

AI代码审查仍是审查

AI code review tools are just buying us time. If AI writes the code and AI reviews it, why do we need a pretty review UI to display that? As much as AI code reviews can be valuable, these will shift left in the dev cycle. There's no reason to waste CI resources and manage versioning in between the review cycles.

AI代码审查工具只是在为我们争取时间。如果AI编写代码且AI审查代码，我们为什么需要一个漂亮的审查UI来展示这些？尽管AI代码审查可能很有价值，但这些将会向开发周期的左侧移动（shift left）。没有理由浪费CI（持续集成，Continuous Integration）资源，也没有理由在审查周期之间管理版本控制。

Post-PR review made sense when humans wrote code and needed fresh eyes. When agents write code, "fresh eyes" is just another agent with the same blind spots. The value is in the iteration loop here, not as an approval gate.

当人类编写代码并需要新鲜视角时，PR后的审查是有意义的。当智能体（agents）编写代码时，"新鲜视角"只是另一个具有相同盲点的智能体。价值在于迭代循环，而非作为批准门槛。

We know from experience agents are not always reliable, and it's very human to think, I caught the AI doing something dumb once; therefore, I must always check it. That instinct made sense when manual verification was feasible. At the current scale, it's not anymore. And it's just going to get worse.

根据经验，我们知道智能体并不总是可靠的，而且人类很容易这样想：我曾经发现AI做过蠢事；因此，我必须始终检查它。当人工验证可行时，这种本能是合理的。在当前规模下，这已不再可行。而且情况只会越来越糟。

From reviewing Code to reviewing Intent

从审查代码到审查意图

The answer is to move the human checkpoint upstream. If the thought of not reviewing code seems scary, let me remind you that checkpoints have moved before in software development. We moved from waterfall sign-offs to continuous integration. We can move them again.

答案是将人类检查点向上游移动。如果不去审查代码的想法听起来很可怕，让我提醒你，检查点在软件开发中已经移动过。我们从瀑布式签字转向了持续集成。我们可以再次移动它们。

Spec-driven development is becoming the main way of working with AI. Humans should review specs, plans, constraints, and acceptance criteria—not 500-line diffs.

规范驱动开发（Spec-driven development）正在成为与AI协作的主要工作方式。人类应该审查规范（specs）、计划、约束和验收标准——而不是500行的代码差异。

In this new paradigm, Specs become the source of truth. Code becomes an artifact of the spec. You don't need to review the code. You review the steps. You review the verification rules. You review the contract the code must fulfill.

在这种新范式中，规范（Specs）成为事实的来源（source of truth）。代码成为规范的产物（artifact）。你不需要审查代码。你审查步骤。你审查验证规则。你审查代码必须履行的契约。

Human-in-the-loop approval moves from "Did you write this correctly?" to "Are we solving the right problem with the right constraints?" The most valuable human judgment is exercised before the first line of code is generated, not after.

人在回路（Human-in-the-loop）的批准从"你写得正确吗？"转变为"我们是否在用正确的约束解决正确的问题？"最有价值的人类判断是在第一行代码生成之前行使的，而不是之后。

Building trust through layers

通过分层建立信任

How comfortable do we need to get before we stop reading the code?

在停止阅读代码之前，我们需要感到多么放心？

In rule form:
Code must not be written by humans
Code must not be reviewed by humans
规则形式：
代码不得由人类编写
代码不得由人类审查
LLMs are not great at following commands. They deviate. Frequently. And they're unreliable at self-verification—they'll confidently tell you the code works while it's on fire. The fix isn't to ask the LLM to verify. It's to ask it to write a script that verifies. Shift from judgment to artifact.

LLM（大语言模型，Large Language Models）并不擅长遵循命令。它们会偏离。频繁地。而且它们在自我验证方面不可靠——它们会自信地告诉你代码运行正常，而实际上代码正在崩溃。解决办法不是让LLM去验证。而是让它编写一个验证脚本。从判断（judgment）转向产物（artifact）。

Trust is layered. This is the Swiss-cheese model: no single gate catches everything. You stack imperfect filters until the holes don't align. So, where else can we put approval gates?

信任是分层的。这就是瑞士奶酪模型（Swiss-cheese model）：没有单一门槛能捕获所有问题。你堆叠不完美的过滤器，直到孔洞不再对齐。那么，我们还可以在哪里设置批准门槛呢？

Layer 1: Compare Multiple Options

层级1：比较多个选项

Instead of asking one agent to get it right, ask three agents to try differently and pick the best outcome. Let them compete. The cost of optionality is the lowest in the history of software engineering.

与其让一个智能体做对，不如让三个智能体以不同方式尝试并选择最佳结果。让它们竞争。在软件工程历史上，可选项（optionality）的成本从未如此之低。

The selection doesn't have to be manual either. You can rank outputs by which one passes the most verification steps, which one produces the smallest diff, which one doesn't introduce new dependencies. Competition creates a signal you wouldn't get from a single attempt.

选择也不必是手动的。你可以根据哪个输出通过了最多的验证步骤、哪个产生的差异最小、哪个没有引入新的依赖关系来对输出进行排序。竞争创造了一个你不会从单一尝试中获得的信号。

Layer 2: Deterministic Guardrails

层级2：确定性护栏

There should be a deterministic way to verify the work. Tests, type checks, contract verification - things that don't have opinions, just facts.

应该有一种确定性的方式来验证工作。测试、类型检查、契约验证（contract verification）——这些没有主观意见，只有事实。

Instead of asking an LLM "Did this work?" you define verification steps that produce a series of pass/fail artifacts. The agent can't negotiate with a failing test. It either meets the specification or it doesn't.

与其问LLM"这行得通吗？"，不如你定义产生一系列通过/失败产物的验证步骤。智能体无法与失败的测试协商。它要么符合规范，要么不符合。

These guardrails can be defined as layers themselves:
  • Coding guidelines- these can be custom linters
  • Organization-wide invariants- the non-negotiables, e.g. No hardcoded credentials, API keys, or tokens
  • Domain Contracts- specific to a framework, a service, or a part of the code base, e.g. Payments domain: All amounts use the Money type
  • Acceptance Criteria- specific to the task

这些护栏本身可以作为层级来定义：

  • 编码规范（Coding guidelines）——这些可以是自定义的linter
  • 组织级不变量（Organization-wide invariants）——不可协商的底线，例如：禁止硬编码凭证、API密钥或令牌
  • 领域契约（Domain Contracts）——特定于框架、服务或代码库某部分，例如：支付领域：所有金额使用Money类型
  • 验收标准（Acceptance Criteria）——特定于任务

Verification steps should be defined before the code is written, not invented after to confirm what's already there. If the agent writes both the code and the tests, you've just moved the problem—now you're trusting the agent to test the right things. Verification criteria need to come from the spec, not from the implementation.

验证步骤应该在代码编写之前定义，而不是在之后发明出来确认已存在的东西。如果智能体既写代码又写测试，你只是转移了问题——现在你在信任智能体去测试正确的东西。验证标准需要来自规范，而不是来自实现。

Layer 4: Humans define acceptance criteria

层级4：人类定义验收标准

So where do humans add value? Upstream, defining what success looks like.

那么人类在哪里增加价值？在上游，定义成功是什么样子。

This is where Behavior-Driven Development becomes newly relevant. BDD was always a good idea—write specifications in natural language that describe expected behavior, then automate those specs as tests. But it never fully caught on because writing specs felt like extra work when you were also going to write the code.

这就是行为驱动开发（Behavior-Driven Development，BDD）重新变得相关的地方。BDD一直是个好主意——用自然语言编写描述预期行为的规范，然后将这些规范自动化为测试。但它从未完全流行起来，因为当你还要编写代码时，编写规范感觉像是额外的工作。

With agents, the equation flips. The spec isn't extra work; it's the primary artifact. You write:

有了智能体，等式翻转了。规范不是额外工作；它是主要产物。你编写：

The agent implements. The BDD framework verifies. You never have to read the implementation unless something fails.

智能体实现。BDD框架验证。除非有东西失败，否则你永远不必阅读实现。

This is humans doing what humans are good at: defining what "correct" means, encoding business logic and edge cases, thinking about what could go wrong. The agent handles the translation from intent to code. The BDD specs become your verification layer—deterministic, automated, and defined before the first line is written.

这是人类做人类擅长的事：定义"正确"意味着什么，编码业务逻辑和边界情况，思考可能出错的地方。智能体处理从意图到代码的转换。BDD规范成为你的验证层——确定性的、自动化的，并在第一行代码编写之前定义。

Acceptance criteria authored by humans, verified by machines. That's the gate that actually matters.

由人类编写、由机器验证的验收标准。这才是真正重要的门槛。

Layer 5: Permission Systems as Architecture

层级5：权限系统即架构

What can this agent touch? What requires escalation? These become architectural decisions, not afterthoughts.

这个智能体能接触什么？什么需要升级处理？这些成为架构决策，而不是事后考虑。

Most agent frameworks treat permissions as an all-or-nothing setting. The agent either has shell access or it doesn't. But granularity matters. An agent fixing a bug in a utility function doesn't need access to your infrastructure configs. An agent writing tests doesn't need to modify CI pipelines.

大多数智能体框架将权限视为全有或全无的设置。智能体要么有shell访问权限，要么没有。但粒度很重要。修复工具函数中bug的智能体不需要访问你的基础设施配置。编写测试的智能体不需要修改CI管道。

Scope should be as narrow as possible while still letting the agent do useful work. If the task is "fix the date parsing bug in utils/dates.py," the agent's filesystem access should be limited to that file and its test file. Not the whole codebase. Not "src/ and tests/". Just the files that matter for this task.

范围应尽可能狭窄，同时仍让智能体完成有用的工作。如果任务是"修复utils/dates.py中的日期解析bug"，智能体的文件系统访问应限制在该文件及其测试文件。不是整个代码库。不是"src/和tests/"。只是对该任务重要的文件。

Escalation triggers are equally important. Certain patterns—touching auth logic, modifying database schemas, adding new dependencies—should automatically flag for human review regardless of how confident the agent is.

升级触发器（Escalation triggers）同样重要。某些模式——触及认证逻辑、修改数据库模式、添加新依赖——应该自动标记为人类审查，无论智能体多么自信。

Layer 6: Adversarial Verification

层级6：对抗性验证

Separation of responsibilities: One agent does the work, another verifies. They don't trust each other, and that's the point.

职责分离：一个智能体做工作，另一个验证。它们互不信任，这正是关键所在。

This is an old pattern—it's why your QA team shouldn't report to your engineering manager, and why the person who writes the code shouldn't be the only one who reviews it.

这是一个古老的模式——这就是为什么你的QA团队不应该向工程经理汇报，以及为什么编写代码的人不应该是唯一审查它的人。

With agents, you can enforce this architecturally. The coding agent has no knowledge of what the verification agent will check. The verification agent has no ability to modify the code to make its own job easier. They're adversarial by design.

有了智能体，你可以在架构层面强制执行这一点。编码智能体不知道验证智能体将检查什么。验证智能体无法修改代码以使自己的工作更容易。它们按设计就是对抗性的。

You can take this further: a third agent attempts to break what the first agent built, specifically targeting edge cases and failure modes. Red team, blue team—but automated and running on every change.

你可以更进一步：第三个智能体试图破坏第一个智能体构建的东西，专门针对边界情况和故障模式。红队、蓝队——但自动化并在每次变更时运行。

Conclusions: What "good code" looks like is changing

结论："好代码"的定义正在改变

The incentive of an agentic system is simple: given a task, can I complete it? Can I please the person who gave it to me? The agent's success is never inherently driven by long-term accuracy or business requirements.

智能体系统（agentic system）的动机很简单：给定一个任务，我能完成它吗？我能让分配任务的人满意吗？智能体的成功从来不是由长期准确性或业务需求内在驱动的。

It's our job to encode in the constraints.

我们的职责是将这些编码进约束中。

For code generated by agents and read by agents, what "good code" looks like will become more standardized. For a new codebase, you'll have to provide less direction because the defaults will be more consistent.

对于由智能体生成并由智能体阅读的代码，"好代码"的样子将变得更加标准化。对于新代码库，你将不得不提供更少的指导，因为默认值将更加一致。

The future is ship fast, observe everything, revert faster.

未来是快速发布、全面观察、更快回滚。

Not: review slowly, miss bugs anyway, debug in production.

而不是：缓慢审查、仍然漏掉bug、在生产环境中调试。

We're not going to outread the machines. We need to outthink them—upstream, where the decisions actually matter. Ultimately, if agents can handle the code just fine, what does it matter if we can read it or not?

我们无法在阅读量上超过机器。我们需要在它们之前思考——在上游，决策真正重要的地方。最终，如果智能体能很好地处理代码，我们能否阅读它又有什么关系呢？

She gives agents their own identities, separate data access, and communication channels—never full access to her email or accounts. Progressive trust is the model: start limited, expand as the agent proves reliable.

  • 将 AI agent（AI代理）视为新员工，而非你自身的延伸。Jesse 的整个代理管理哲学源自她招聘员工的经验。她为代理分配独立的身份、单独的数据访问权限和通信渠道——从不授予对其电子邮件或账户的完全访问权限。渐进式信任是模型：从受限开始，随着代理证明其可靠性而逐步扩展权限。

  • Physical partitioning is a real security strategy. Running each agent on its own Mac Mini sounds extreme, but it solves a real problem: preventing one agent from accidentally leaking sensitive data through another agent's communication channel. The finance agent can read bank statements but can't text anyone. The scheduling agent can text, but has no financial data. This is a practical framework anyone managing multiple agents should think through.

  • Physical partitioning（物理分区）是一种真正的安全策略。在每个Mac Mini上运行单个代理听起来极端，但这解决了一个实际问题：防止一个代理通过另一个代理的通信通道意外泄露敏感数据。财务代理可以读取银行对账单但不能发送短信。日程代理可以发短信，但没有财务数据。这是任何管理多个代理的人都应该考虑的实用框架。

  • Photos are the most underrated input for AI agents. Jesse's core workflow is shockingly simple: take a photo, send it to the agent, get structured output. She photographs lesson activities, book pages, physical supplies, and curriculum materials. The agent handles all the heavy lifting of logging, categorizing, and connecting that information. No typing, no structured input—just photos.

  • 照片是 AI agents（AI代理）最被低估的输入方式。Jesse 的核心工作流简单得令人惊讶：拍照，发送给代理，获得结构化输出。她拍摄课程活动、书页、实物用品和课程材料的照片。代理处理记录、分类和连接这些信息的所有繁重工作。无需打字，无需结构化输入——只需照片。

  • You don't need to be technical to build real software with a coding agent. Jesse had never opened a terminal before six months ago. With Cole, her coding agent, she built a custom kids' TV app, iterated over four days, and deployed it to a Google TV Streamer. Her approach: describe what you want, push back when the agent says something isn't possible, and keep going.

  • 无需技术背景也能用 coding agent（编程代理）构建真正的软件。Jesse 六个月前从未打开过终端。通过 Cole（她的编程代理），她构建了一个自定义儿童电视应用，历时四天迭代，并部署到了 Google TV Streamer（谷歌电视流媒体设备）。她的方法是：描述你想要什么，当代理说某事不可能时坚持己见，然后继续推进。

  • Inventory your physical world so AI can reach into it. One of Jesse's most powerful moves was photographing all her educational supplies and having Sylvie build an inventory. Now when she asks for a lesson plan, the agent can say, "Also, pull out the tracing board from the cupboard." This bridges the gap between the digital agent and the physical world in a way that's immediately useful.

  • 盘点你的物理世界，让 AI 能够触及其中。Jesse 最有力的举措之一是拍摄她所有的教育用品并让 Sylvie 建立库存。现在当她要求制定教案时，代理可以说："还有，从橱柜里拿出描图板。"这以一种立即有用的方式弥合了数字代理与物理世界之间的差距。

  • Use "decision files" to prevent agents from relitigating settled questions. Jesse maintains a decisions file in Obsidian that each agent knows about. When she makes a final call, she flags it, and the agent knows not to revisit it. This is a simple, powerful pattern for anyone dealing with agents that keep second-guessing or re-asking about things you've already resolved.

  • 使用"decision files"（决策文件）防止代理对已解决的问题反复纠结。Jesse 在 Obsidian（一款笔记软件）中维护一个决策文件，每个代理都知道它的存在。当她做出最终决定时，她会标记它，代理就知道不要重新讨论。对于任何正在处理那些不断对已经解决的问题进行二次猜测或重复询问的代理的人来说，这是一个简单而强大的模式。

item.title: [翻译] Simon Willison: 基于 WebAssembly 和 Gifsicle 的 GIF 优化工具
item.description:
标签: #GIF优化 #WebAssembly #AI编程 #网页工具

摘要: 作者借助Claude Code将C语言编写的Gifsicle编译为WebAssembly，构建了一个纯浏览器端的GIF优化工具，支持可视化预览不同压缩设置并手动调整参数。

原标题: GIF optimization tool using WebAssembly and Gifsicle

Agentic Engineering Patterns

Agentic Engineering Patterns

智能体工程模式（Agentic Engineering Patterns）

I like to include animated GIF demos in my online writing, often recorded using LICEcap. There's an example in the Interactive explanations chapter.

我喜欢在在线文章中加入动画 GIF（animated GIF）演示，通常使用 LICEcap 录制。在《Interactive explanations》章节中有一个例子。

These GIFs can be pretty big. I've tried a few tools for optimizing GIF file size and my favorite is Gifsicle by Eddie Kohler. It compresses GIFs by identifying regions of frames that have not changed and storing only the differences, and can optionally reduce the GIF color palette or apply visible lossy compression for greater size reductions.

这些 GIF 文件可能非常大。我尝试过多种优化 GIF 文件大小的工具，最喜欢的是 Eddie Kohler 开发的 Gifsicle。它通过识别帧之间未变化的区域并仅存储差异来压缩 GIF，还可以选择减少 GIF 调色板或应用可见的有损压缩（lossy compression）以进一步减小体积。

Gifsicle is written in C and the default interface is a command line tool. I wanted a web interface so I could access it in my browser and visually preview and compare the different settings.

Gifsicle 使用 C 语言编写，默认界面是一个命令行工具（command line tool）。我需要一个网页界面（web interface），这样我可以在浏览器中访问它，并直观地预览和比较不同设置的效果。

I prompted Claude Code for web (from my iPhone using the Claude iPhone app) against my simonw/tools repo with the following:

我通过 iPhone 上的 Claude 应用向 Claude Code 发送了网页开发提示词，针对我的 simonw/tools 代码库，内容如下：

Here's what it built, plus an animated GIF demo that I optimized using the tool:

以下是它构建的工具，以及我使用该工具优化的动画 GIF（animated GIF）演示：

Let's address that prompt piece by piece.

让我们逐段分析这个提示词。

gif-optimizer.html
gif-optimizer.html

gif-optimizer.html

The first line simply tells it the name of the file I want to create. Just a filename is enough here - I know that when Claude runs "ls" on the repo it will understand that every file is a different tool.

第一行只是告诉它我想创建的文件名。这里只需要一个文件名就足够了——我知道当 Claude 在代码库上运行 "ls" 时，它会明白每个文件代表一个不同的工具。

My simonw/tools repo currently lacks a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md file. I've found that agents pick up enough of the gist of the repo just from scanning the existing file tree and looking at relevant code in existing files.

我的 simonw/tools 代码库目前缺少 CLAUDE.md 或 AGENTS.md 文件。我发现智能体（agents）仅通过扫描现有的文件树和查看现有文件中的相关代码，就能掌握代码库的要旨。

Compile gifsicle to WASM, then build a web page that lets you open or drag-drop an animated GIF onto it and it then shows you that GIF compressed using gifsicle with a number of different settings, each preview with the size and a download button
Compile gifsicle to WASM, then build a web page that lets you open or drag-drop an animated GIF onto it and it then shows you that GIF compressed using gifsicle with a number of different settings, each preview with the size and a download button

将 gifsicle 编译为 WASM（WebAssembly），然后构建一个网页，允许你打开或拖拽（drag-drop）动画 GIF 到页面上，然后展示使用 gifsicle 以多种不同设置压缩后的 GIF，每个预览都显示文件大小并提供下载按钮

I'm making a bunch of assumptions here about Claude's existing knowledge, all of which paid off.

这里我对 Claude 的现有知识做了许多假设，而这些假设都得到了验证。

Gifsicle is nearly 30 years old now and is a widely used piece of software - I was confident that referring to it by name would be enough for Claude to find the code.

Gifsicle 已有近 30 年历史，是一款广泛使用的软件——我有信心仅通过名称提及就足以让 Claude 找到相关代码。

"Compile gifsicle to WASM" is doing a lot of work here.

"将 gifsicle 编译为 WASM" 这句话在这里承担了大量工作。

WASM is short for WebAssembly, the technology that lets browsers run compiled code safely in a sandbox.

WASM 是 WebAssembly 的缩写，这项技术让浏览器能够在沙箱（sandbox）中安全地运行编译后的代码。

Compiling a project like Gifsicle to WASM is not a trivial operation, involving a complex toolchain usually involving the Emscripten project. It often requires a lot of trial and error to get everything working.

将像 Gifsicle 这样的项目编译为 WASM 并非易事，涉及复杂的工具链（toolchain），通常需要使用 Emscripten 项目。这通常需要大量的反复试验才能一切正常运行。

Coding agents are fantastic at trial and error! They can often brute force their way to a solution where I would have given up after the fifth inscrutable compiler error.

编程智能体（Coding agents）非常擅长反复试验！它们通常能够通过暴力尝试找到解决方案，而我在遇到第五个难以理解的编译器错误时可能就已经放弃了。

I've seen Claude Code figure out WASM builds many times before, so I was quite confident this would work.

我以前多次看到 Claude Code 解决 WASM 构建问题，因此我相当确信这次也能成功。

"then build a web page that lets you open or drag-drop an animated GIF onto it" describes a pattern I've used in a lot of my other tools.

"然后构建一个允许你打开或拖拽（drag-drop）动画 GIF 到页面上的网页"描述的是我在许多其他工具中使用过的模式。

HTML file uploads work fine for selecting files, but a nicer UI, especially on desktop, is to allow users to drag and drop files into a prominent drop zone on a page.

HTML 文件上传对于选择文件来说工作正常，但更好的用户界面（UI），尤其是在桌面端，是允许用户将文件拖放到页面上显眼的放置区域（drop zone）中。

Setting this up involves a bit of JavaScript to process the events and some CSS for the drop zone. It's not complicated but it's enough extra work that I might not normally add it myself. With a prompt it's almost free.

设置这个功能需要一些 JavaScript 来处理事件，以及一些 CSS 来美化放置区域。这并不复杂，但额外的工作量足以让我通常不会自己添加它。但使用提示词的话，这几乎是零成本的。

Here's the resulting UI - which was influenced by Claude taking a peek at my existing image-resize-quality tool:

这是最终的 UI——它受到了 Claude 查看我现有的 image-resize-quality 工具的影响：

I didn't ask for the GIF URL input and I'm not keen on it, because it only works against URLs to GIFs that are served with open CORS headers. I'll probably remove that in a future update.

我并没有要求添加 GIF URL 输入功能，而且我也不太喜欢它，因为它只适用于带有开放 CORS（跨域资源共享）标头提供的 GIF URL。我可能会在未来的更新中移除这个功能。

"then shows you that GIF compressed using gifsicle with a number of different settings, each preview with the size and a download button" describes the key feature of the application.
